description: One record per public research work; verified version metadata plus a bounded editorial evidence guide. This custom JSON catalog does not claim a standard JSON-LD schema.
author: Jack Chen
scope: Four abstract computational preprints. Versions, endpoints, stored-output checks and reused cohorts are not additional independent papers or replications.
discoverability_limit: Public readable text, stable identifiers and structured metadata help access; no guarantee of search indexing, citations or future AI training inclusion is made.

works.title: Available regulatory mutation directions improve finite-budget adaptation from matched states in a developmental-network model
works.license_note: Zenodo lists CC-BY-4.0 for its deposited manuscript. The linked GitHub RIGHTS_STATUS.md says no project license is granted; no software license or tagged GitHub release was found. This catalog does not extend the deposit license to repository code.
works.model: 16-trait developmental-network model; matched trained states and a fixed proposal budget
works.question: Does access to more adjustable regulatory directions improve subsequent adaptation from the same starting state?
works.principal_bounded_finding: More available directions improved the fixed primary and matched opening/freezing contrasts under the tested constraints.
adverse_or_unresolved: Tighter tested bounds attenuated some paired capacity contrasts.
Target attainment remained rare in difficult cases; cost and historical retention did not improve uniformly.
The results do not establish spontaneous origin, maintenance by selection or a universal dimensionality advantage.
works.reuse_and_replication_boundary: The record distinguishes an initial separate 48-unit cohort and a later 48-unit-per-family validation. Multiple endpoints and intervention contrasts are not independent replications.

works.title: Population state changes the transfer value of organized variation in a finite-population model
works.license_note: Manuscript, figures and data: CC-BY-4.0. Original code: MIT; third-party terms remain separate.
works.model: Two-dimensional finite-population model; organized versus quarter-turned variation with equal covariance eigenvalues
works.question: How does current population state change the transfer value of an inherited variation orientation?
works.principal_bounded_finding: Both centroid and centered population configuration changed later rule effects. Prospective state-based choices improved on centroid-only choices in fresh histories.
adverse_or_unresolved: The improvement was below the prespecified usefulness target; unconditional switching was already strong and subgroup harms remained.
More detailed local calculations improved one-step calibration but worsened terminal calibration.
Neither a unique mediator nor a generally optimal policy is identified.
works.reuse_and_replication_boundary: The prospective policy comparison uses 48 freshly trained histories. Independent continuations from fixed checkpoints test conditional responses; they are not additional independently trained cohorts.

works.title: Retained memory and fresh exploration under a matched evaluation budget in a changing-target population model
works.license_note: Manuscript, figures and data: CC-BY-4.0. Original code: MIT; third-party terms remain separate.
works.model: 32-bit, 32-individual changing-target model; a shared four-record cache and matched objective-query budget
works.question: When does retained history improve population search relative to current donors, new children or fresh scouts?
works.principal_bounded_finding: Memory value depended on the comparator and recurrence. A fixed hybrid benefited from historical rather than current donors with scouting held fixed.
adverse_or_unresolved: The independent cohort only partly reproduced the complete cumulative ranking-switch prediction.
Memory lost to random scouts under independent targets; terminal comparisons and individual failures qualify average gains.
An imposed search policy does not demonstrate selection for memory or its spontaneous origin.
works.reuse_and_replication_boundary: The second cohort supports the recurrence interaction and independent-target disadvantage but leaves recurrent cumulative superiority unresolved. Hybrid and retention comparisons reuse that already observed cohort.

works.title: Environmental recurrence changes the transmission advantage of private memory in a finite-budget population model
works.license_note: Manuscript, figures and data: CC-BY-4.0. Original code: MIT; third-party terms remain separate.
works.model: 32-bit, 32-individual finite-budget model; private one-record caches, inherited policy labels and founder identities; separate 061 two-individual/one-bit stationary model with supplied storage and ongoing symmetric policy switching
works.question: When does using an available private memory increase founder representation, and does population accuracy change in the same way?
works.principal_bounded_finding: Future recurrence increased the matched historical-use founder effect at fixed prepared states; a new cohort reproduced its direction. A fixed interacting objective retained a positive recurrence effect. The separate stationary model certifies a small +0.458222476-point recurrence effect on H frequency.
adverse_or_unresolved: Frequent founder loss and adverse population outcomes remain; founder representation is distinct from collective accuracy.
The pulse population-accuracy primary and bounded-observation noise interaction remain unresolved. Noise lowered average true accuracy.
No noise equivalence, equilibrium invasion, spontaneous memory origin or general costly advantage is established.

In the separate stationary model, active-minus-neutral accuracy is adverse under ZERO and positive under HALF; numerical enclosures are not confidence intervals or stationary evidence for the 32-individual model.
works.reuse_and_replication_boundary: Studies046,052 and057 contain separately identified independent-cohort tests. Studies059 and060 reuse057 preparations;058 has new paired objective-specific inputs. Releases1.0–1.5 are versions of one work, not separate replications. Study061 is a distinct mathematical model, not a new empirical replication.
